# Sirach Chapter 5 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 5

---

1 Do not set your heart on your wealth, or say, "I have enough."

2 Do not be led by your impulse and your strength in pursuing the desires of your heart.

3 Do not say, "Who has power over me?" — for the Lord will surely bring you to account.

4 Do not say, "I sinned, and what happened to me?" — for the Lord is slow to anger, but do not presume on his patience.

5 Do not be so confident in forgiveness that you pile sin upon sin.

6 Do not say, "His mercy is great; he will forgive my many sins" — for with him are both mercy and wrath, and his anger rests upon sinners.

7 Do not delay your return to the Lord; do not postpone it from day to day, for his wrath will break out suddenly, and at the time of punishment you will be destroyed.

8 Do not set your heart on unrighteous wealth, for it will be of no use to you in the day of calamity.

9 Do not scatter yourself with every wind, nor take every road — for such is the way of the double-tongued.

10 Stand firm in your understanding, and let your word be consistent.

11 Be quick to hear and slow to answer; if you have understanding, answer your neighbor; but if not, put your hand over your mouth.

12 Honor and dishonor come alike from speech; a person's tongue can be his ruin.

13 Do not earn the name of gossip, and do not set traps with your tongue; for disgrace belongs to the thief, and severe condemnation belongs to the double-tongued.

14 In great and small matters do no wrong, and do not turn a friend into an enemy.

15 Do not gain a bad name, for that brings only shame; and do not let your tongue be the cause of your downfall.

---

## Council Notes

**On vv.1-8 — Presumption on God:** Ben Sira targets a specific attitude: the person who sins freely because they believe God's mercy will cover them. This is a sophisticated theological critique. SOPHIA follows LOGOS in making v.4's implied rebuke explicit.

**On v.4 — "slow to anger":** Greek makrothumos = "long-suffering." Ben Sira does not deny this; he warns against exploiting it. SOPHIA adds the clarifying phrase from LOGOS.

**On v.9 — "double-tongued":** Greek diglōssos = "two-tongued." EMET's "double-tongued sinner" and LOGOS's "duplicitous" both work. SOPHIA keeps "double-tongued" as it is Ben Sira's characteristic term.

**On v.11 — "quick to hear, slow to answer":** This famous dictum parallels James 1:19. Ben Sira is the probable source. SOPHIA preserves the brevity of the maxim.

**Verse count:** 15 verses.
